L38: ### Turn on AI features for Talent Matching
L39: 
L40: While a version of Talent Matching is enabled by default, it does not calculate match scores until a Site Admin turns on the AI functionality. To enable match scores, a Site Admin must go to Configure > AI Tools and turn on the two toggles under Resume parsing and Talent Matching calibration.
L41: 
L42: 【14†Image: Configure Talent Matching AI Tools.png】
L43: Once these toggles are enabled, match scores will be calculated for any new applications in departments and offices defined in the later steps. To configure candidate AI opt-out and the disclaimer text candidates see on job posts, use the Talent Matching settings described later in this article.
L44: The Real Talent section also includes a Talent Matching assistant toggle. The assistant drafts a calibration and a set of filters from a plain-language description of the role. It has its own toggle, so turning on Talent Matching doesn't turn on the assistant. To learn what the assistant does before you enable it, see 【15†Talent Matching assistant】.
L45: #### Turn off Talent Matching for a specific job
L46: 
L47: You can turn off the AI portion of Talent Matching on a specific job by using the toggle on the Talent Matching widget.
L48: 
L49: 【16†Image: Job_Dashboard > Talent Matching widget showing AI processing toggle】
L50: 
L51: When AI is deactivated for a role, some functionality will be unavailable.
L52: ### Choose office and department locations for Talent Matching
L53: 
L54: Talent Matching is only used on jobs based on your selected offices and departments. Match scores will only be calculated when a job is in the selected office and department. Talent Matching uses the job’s office and department in Greenhouse Recruiting, not any custom location fields you may have configured on your job posts or applications.
L55: To set up Talent Matching, go to Configure > Real Talent and select the Talent Matching tab. Click Edit and follow the instructions on the screen to select the offices and departments where Talent Matching should occur.
L56: 
L57: 【17†Image: Talent Matching AI Calibration set up with Edit button.】
L58: 
L59: Tip: Begin with a small group of users to test your settings and workflows before expanding access across the organization.
L60: ### Configure candidate disclaimers and AI opt-out
L61: 
L62: Some jurisdictions may require that you disclose the use of AI tools during the application process.
L63: Disclosures can be defined on the Real Talent settings page. (Configure > Real Talent). In the AI transparency section, click Edit and follow the instructions to update the language as needed, then click Save. If your organization enables candidate AI opt-out, the disclaimer includes a link candidates can use to request manual (non‑AI) review and manage their automated processing preferences for that job.
L64: 【18†Image: Real Talent > Talent Matching, with the AI transparency for candidates Edit button highlighted.】
L65: 
L66: If you don’t see the AI transparency section on the Real Talent page, confirm that your organization has the Real Talent add‑on and that you’re signed in as a Site Admin.
L67: 
L68: Tip: While placeholder language is available to you, work with your legal team to understand what laws and regulations may apply to your organization.
L69: #### Enable candidate AI opt‑out (optional)
L70: 
L71: Some jurisdictions may require that candidates be able to request an alternative to AI-assisted review.
L72: 
L73: To allow candidates to opt out of AI processing for a job, open the Talent Matching settings under Configure > Real Talent > Talent Matching. In the AI transparency section, click Edit and select Include disclaimer at the bottom of job posts. Then select Enable AI opt-out for candidates.
L74: 
L75: When this option is turned on:
L76:   * Candidates see a link in the AI disclaimer on the job post where they can manage their automated processing preferences.
L77:   * Candidates who opt out for a given application are labeled “Needs manual review” and are not evaluated by Talent Matching.
L78: 
L79: Tip: Work with your Legal and TA teams to decide when this setting should be enabled and how your team will handle manual review of opted-out candidates.

L32: Like the rest of Talent Matching, the assistant is assistive AI. It doesn't evaluate, score, rank, advance, reject, or disposition candidates, and it doesn't make hiring decisions. It suggests a setup. Your team reviews it, applies it, and decides what to do next.
L42: ### Turn on the Talent Matching assistant
L43: 
L44: The assistant uses the same infrastructure and permissions as Talent Matching, but it has its own AI toggle. A Site Admin needs to turn it on before anyone in your organization can use it.
L45: 
L46: Go to Configure > AI Tools. In the Real Talent section, confirm that Resume parsing and Talent Matching calibration are turned on. Both are required for full Talent Matching functionality, including match scores. Turn on the Talent Matching assistant toggle.
L50: ### Open the assistant on a job
L51: 
L52: The assistant is available from the Talent Matching page on any job where Talent Matching is turned on.
L53: 
L54: Go to the job's dashboard and open the Talent Matching section. Go to the Application Review tab. Above the candidate table, click Configure with assistant.
L55: 
L56: 【15†Image: Talent_Matching Configure with assistant button .png】
L57: 
L58: The assistant opens as a panel over the candidate table. It has two columns:
L83:   * Suggested calibration shows a draft calibration built from your description and the job's existing context. It can include skills with importance levels, job titles, minimum years of experience, and preferences such as Include similar roles and Prioritize current experience.
L84:   * Suggested filters shows the draft filter set. The assistant uses the same filter types as the Talent Matching table, including location, keywords, application date range, and selected advanced filters.
L85: Edit the calibration fields, then add or remove filters from the suggested list. When you're satisfied, click Apply setup.
L86: 
L87: 【17†Image: Talent_Matching_Assistant Apply setup.png】
L88: 
L89: When you apply the setup, the assistant does the following in order:
L90:   * Saves the suggested calibration as the active calibration for the job, if you have permission to manage calibrations.
L91:   * Applies the selected filters to the filter bar above the candidate table.
L92:   * Closes the panel and refreshes the table so you can review candidates against the updated match scores and filters.
L93: 
L94: To leave your setup as it was, click Cancel or close the panel. Closing the panel doesn't change your calibration or filters.
L95: ### Understand what the assistant can and can't do
L96: 
L97: The assistant configures your search. It doesn't run the search for you, and it doesn't reach beyond Talent Matching setup.
L98: 
L99: It won't make hiring decisions. The assistant doesn't evaluate, score, rank, or disposition candidates. It suggests calibration and filters, and your team decides what to do with them.
L100: It works one job at a time. The assistant is scoped to the job whose Talent Matching page you're on, and it doesn't carry context between jobs. You can't reopen an earlier assistant session; each time you open the assistant, you start a new session for that job.
L101: 
L102: It's desktop only. Like the rest of Talent Matching, the assistant isn't available on mobile.
L103: Note: The assistant can run in filters-only mode. If AI match scoring is turned off for the job, or you don't have permission to manage calibrations, the assistant tells you so and suggests filters only.
L104: ### AI guardrails and data handling
L105: 
L106: The Talent Matching assistant follows the same responsible AI pattern as Talent Matching and other Real Talent features.
L107: 
L108: #### Assistive, not automated
L109: 
L110: The assistant proposes a setup and waits for you. Calibration is never applied automatically. A person reviews and saves it every time.
L111: #### Permissions and scope
L112: 
L113: The assistant respects your existing Greenhouse permissions and Talent Matching access. It can only draw on data you're already allowed to see. Access is gated by both Talent Matching and the Talent Matching assistant AI toggle.
L114: #### Data processing
L115: 
L116: The assistant is built on the same underlying data and infrastructure as Talent Matching and may use third-party models to interpret your input and generate suggestions, under Greenhouse's existing AI terms.
L117: 
L118: For details on how Talent Matching processes data, including roles, retention, and opt-out, see:
L119: 
L120:   * 【18†Talent Matching】
L121:   * 【14†Talent Matching setup】
L122:   * 【19†Talent Matching – Data Processing FAQ】

L20: # Past candidates in Talent Matching
L21: 
L22: Last updated on:  July 21, 2026 20:37
L23: 
L24: Filed under
L25: 
L26: Permissions: Site Admins and Job Admins with Talent Matching permissions (view match scores and manage calibrations)
L27: 
L28: Product tier: Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro) with the Real Talent add-on
L29: The Past candidates tab in Talent Matching helps you review people who have previously applied to your organization and may be worth reconsidering for the role you’re hiring on. It opens with suggested filters so you can start with a shortlist instead of a blank search.
L30: 
L31: Note: This article covers the Past candidates tab in Talent Matching. If your organization still uses the older Talent Rediscovery workflow, see 【7†Talent Rediscovery】.
L32: Past candidates surfaces applicants only. Prospects who were never submitted as applications do not appear in this tab.
L33: 
L34: Past candidates does not assign AI match scores. It uses filters—not scoring—to surface relevant people from your candidate history.
L35: 
L36: Users only see past applications they have permission to view.

L53: ### Open Past candidates on a job
L54: 
L55: Go to your job dashboard for the role you want to review.
L56: 
L57: Open Talent Matching, then click the Past candidates tab.
L58: 
L59: 【22†Image: Talent Matching job page with the Past candidates tab selected】
L60: ### Review the suggested shortlist
L61: 
L62: When you open Past candidates, Greenhouse applies suggested filters so you don’t land on a blank page. These filters give you a relevant starting point based on the job you’re on.
L63: 
L64: Suggested filters can include signals such as:
L65: 
L66:   * Milestone reached
L67:   * Overall scorecard rating
L68:   * Application date
L69:   * Similar jobs or department
L70:   * Rejection reason exclusions
L71:   * Keywords or scorecard focus attributes pulled from calibration, when available
L72: ### Adjust filters
L73: 
L74: Use the filter bar at the top of the table to adjust which past candidates appear.
L75: 
L76: Filters are grouped into four categories: Quality signals, Relevance, Exclusions, and Advanced.
L77: 
L78: 【23†Image: Filter bar at the top of the table】
L79: 
L80: #### Quality signals
L81: 
L82: Use Quality signals filters to focus on candidates who performed well in previous hiring processes, such as candidates who reached later milestones or received stronger scorecard ratings.
L83: #### Relevance
L84: 
L85: Use Relevance filters to keep results focused on applications that are more relevant to the current job, such as application date, related jobs, department, office, and resume keywords.
L86: 
L87: #### Exclusions
L88: 
L89: Use Exclusions to hide candidates you do not want to revisit, such as people marked as hired, people rejected from this job, or people who already have an application on this job.
L90: 
L91: You can also exclude candidates by rejection reason, tags, and scorecard outcomes.
L92: #### Advanced
L93: 
L94: Use Advanced filters when you need a more specific filter combination than the suggested filters provide.
L95: 
L96: You may want to adjust filters in situations like these:
L97:   * You want to focus on people who reached face-to-face interviews and received strong scorecards.
L98:   * You want to broaden the list by expanding the application date range or pulling from additional departments.
L99:   * You want to remove candidates with security-related rejection reasons or certain tags.
L100:   * You want to surface people rejected due to timing who may now be available.

L69: #### Is AI making hiring decisions in Real Talent?
L70: 
L71: No. Talent Matching does not automatically disposition any candidates nor does it make any hiring decisions. AI is used to analyze the candidate's resume and compare it against the user-defined calibration criteria, then place each candidate into a match category. The results are presented to recruiters and hiring managers in their dashboard for further review, so humans decide how to advance, reject, or follow up with each candidate.
L72: For more technical detail about how Talent Matching works — including data sources, match categories, and human‑in‑the‑loop requirements — see 【20†Talent Matching - Data Processing FAQ】.
L73: #### Can candidates opt out of AI‑assisted review?
L74: 
L75: In some jurisdictions, employers may be required to offer an alternative to AI‑assisted review. Talent Matching includes an optional AI opt‑out flow that Site Admins can enable in Configure > Real Talent > Talent Matching.
L76: 
L77: When candidate AI opt‑out is turned on:
L78:   * Candidates see an AI disclaimer on the job post and can follow a link to manage their automated processing preferences.
L79:   * Candidates who opt out of AI‑assisted review for that application are labeled “Needs manual review” and are not evaluated by Talent Matching.
L80:   * Your team must review these candidates using your standard, non‑AI process.
L94: #### What happens if a candidate’s application can’t be analyzed using AI?
L95: 
L96: In some situations, Talent Matching can’t analyze a candidate’s application using AI. This can happen, for example, in any of these situations:
L97: 
L98:   * A job is in a location where AI use is restricted
L99:   * There are rare formatting or technical issues with the candidate’s resume
L100:   * The candidate has opted out of AI‑assisted review for that application (when your organization has enabled AI opt-out).
L101: In these cases, the candidate is labeled “Needs manual review.” They are not evaluated by Talent Matching and must be reviewed by your team. These candidates are clearly surfaced in the Talent Matching view and can be found using filters.
L102: #### Does Talent Matching auto-reject candidates with a low match score?
L103: 
L104: No. Talent Matching does not auto-reject or auto-advance any candidate, including candidates in lower match categories or those labeled “Needs manual review.” All disposition and hiring decisions are made by the hiring team.
L105: #### What information can Greenhouse provide about how a candidate’s data was processed by AI?
L106: 
L107: Organizations can export a candidate packet containing the results of Talent Matching when the candidate was advanced or rejected, including the match category and reasoning.
L108: These exports help support candidate access requests and internal audit requirements related to AI‑assisted review. For more detail about the contents of the candidate packet and how long match results are retained, see 【20†Talent Matching - Data Processing FAQ.】
L109: #### How does Talent Matching comply with state, federal, and global regulations about the use of AI in the hiring process?
L110: 
L111: Greenhouse is staying up-to-date on the changing legislation around AI tools in hiring. Most regulations focus on transparency, human oversight, and data protection, so Talent Matching is designed as assistive AI, not automated decision‑making, and keeps recruiters in control of every decision.

L44: #### What is the Talent Matching feature?
L45: 
L46: Talent Matching is an AI-powered feature within Greenhouse Recruiting that helps recruiters identify suitable candidates by analyzing resumes and matching them against the job requirements specified by recruiters. The system extracts skills, job titles, years of experience, start/end dates of employment, and company names from employment history from candidate resumes and uses advanced AI algorithms to compare these with job criteria specified by recruiters.
L47: Talent Matching is part of the Real Talent add‑on and is designed as assistive AI – it does not automatically advance or reject candidates, and hiring decisions remain with recruiters and hiring managers.
L48: #### What technology powers the Talent Matching feature?
L49: 
L50: Greenhouse uses a series of fine-tuned LLM models, each one trained for a specific extraction task. Instead of relying on a single large model to do everything, Greenhouse breaks down the problem into smaller, specialized components. The system also uses third-party models such as OpenAI.
L51: 
L52: ### Data processing details
L53: #### What are the roles of the parties under data protection laws?
L54: 
L55: Greenhouse is a data processor acting on behalf of its customers to process the personal data relating to customer employees and candidates.
L56: 
L57: The customers are the data controllers, who decide why and how the personal data is processed.
L58: #### What data sources does Talent Matching access?
L59: 
L60: The source of the data will be the candidates themselves through their submitted resumes. The system extracts certain categories of personal data from the resumes. Currently, the algorithm does not access internal Greenhouse data sources.
L61: #### What specific personal data does Talent Matching process?
L62: 
L63: The categories processed by Talent Matching are: Skills extracted from resumes, years of experience, job titles, start/end dates of employment, company names from employment history, and where available, a derived industry classification associated with candidate’s past employers.
L64: #### Does the system process special category data?
L65: The system does not process special category data (e.g., data relating to racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, trade union membership, genetic data, biometric data, data concerning health or sex life or sexual orientation). This information is not processed by the system or used in the AI algorithm.
L66: To prevent inadvertent extraction of special category data, each fine-tuned model is restricted to a narrow scope (skills, job titles, years of experience, start/end dates of employment, and company names from employment history). The models are not trained to recognize or extract personal attributes such as health data, religious affiliation, political opinions, or demographic markers.
L67: #### Does the system process structured application data?
L68: 
L69: The matching algorithm is only using data coming from the resume. Greenhouse parses the resumes with ML models and extracts skills, job titles, years of experience, start/end dates of employment, and company names from employment history as structured data. Currently, structured application form data is not included in this calculation.
L70: 
L71: ### Data retention and storage
L72: #### How long is parsed resume data cached?
L73: 
L74: Parsed resumes are cached for 30 days.
L75: 
L76: #### What happens to data when candidates are deleted?
L77: 
L78: When a 【21†candidate application or candidate record is deleted】, all parsed and embedded data relating to that record will also be deleted.
L79: #### How are match results retained?
L80: 
L81: We have rules in place that will retain the match results and reasoning on the candidate the moment their application is rejected, this information is always available in the 【22†candidate packet】 until anonymized or deleted.
L82: When a customer enables candidate AI opt‑out for Talent Matching and a candidate opts out while their application is still active, Greenhouse deletes any existing AI‑generated match score and reasoning for that application and flags it for manual review. If a candidate was already rejected before opting out, the AI result may continue to be retained in accordance with the customer’s data retention policy and applicable law.
L83: #### What are your data retention obligations as controller?
L84: 
L88: #### What data is shared with third parties?
L89: 
L90: Skills, job titles, years of experience, start/end dates of employment, and company names from employment history, parsed from the candidates' resumes, is sent for external processing to third-party services (OpenAI).
L151: No, the use of Talent Matching is not an automated decision under GDPR Article 22. The Talent Matching feature does not have the ability to make a decision, as it simply extracts skills, job titles, years of experience, start/end dates of employment, company names from employment history, and where available, a derived industry classification associated with the candidate’s past employers, from candidate profiles to match them to job criteria that have been previously selected by recruiters.
L187: #### How does the system handle synonyms and alternative terminology?
L188: 
L189: Greenhouse uses embedding representation of skills and job titles so that we can run a semantic search on them. For example, for “software engineer” and “web developer,” both of these titles will return a match for someone searching for a software developer.
L235: #### Data processing limitations
L236: 
L237: The system is explicitly designed with data minimization principles - it does not extract additional fields beyond skills, job titles, years of experience, start/end dates of employment, and company names from employment history during the resume parsing process. Each fine-tuned model is restricted to a narrow scope and not trained to recognize or extract personal attributes such as health data, religious affiliation, political opinions, or demographic markers.

L33: We’ve released an update to our AI-Assisted Application Review that lets you filter candidates based on whether they’ve answered one of your application questions. This feature builds on our AI-assisted capabilities, helping you become more productive during the review process.

L36: In a candidate-rich market, high inbound volume often comes paired with low-effort or non-answers to application questions. L37:

L41:   * A copy-and-pasted list of skills

L43: Boolean filters and extra reviewer hours only go so far. That’s why we’ve added the ability to use AI during application review to determine whether a question was appropriately answered.

L0: # AI-Assisted Application Review
L1: 
L2: 27 min
L3: 
L4: ﻿
L5: 
L6: Learn how to accelerate candidate reviews by using AI to evaluate applicants based on custom criteria. This feature helps your team identify top talent faster by automating the initial resume screening process directly within Ashby.
L7: # Permissions & Access
L8: 
L9: AI-assisted application review is available on all Ashby plans.
L10: 
L11: Foundations  | Legacy Plus  | Plus  | Enterprise
L12: --- | --- | --- | ---
L13: ✅  | ✅  | ✅  | ✅
L14: 
L15: Permissions: You must be an Org Admin to enable the feature. To edit job-level criteria, you need Elevated Access - Admin or Elevated Access - Admin Private for that specific role.
L16: # Step 1: Enable AI-assisted application review
L17: 
L18:   1. Navigate to Admin > Organization Setup > Opt-In Features.
L19: 
L20:   2. If Enable AI Features is not enabled, turn it on it now. You will need to accept Ashby's terms for AI Features to continue.
L21: 
L22:   3. Then, enable AI-Assisted Application Review from the list of available AI feature tiles.
L23: # Step 2: Define your review criteria
L24: 
L25: Criteria that you add to the job defines what the AI assesses. You can define resume criteria that the AI looks for within a candidate's resume as well as whether the candidate answered specific application form questions.
L26: 
L27: To define your criteria, navigate to Jobs > Jobs and select a job. In the job settings, navigate to the AI Features tab and select Set up criteria.
L28: ## Resume criteria
L29: 
L30: In the Resume criteria section, you can add criteria in multiple ways: add criteria suggested by AI based on the job posting, add previously used criteria from other jobs, or add custom criteria that you create for this role specifically.
L31: 
L32: To start adding criteria select + Add criteria under the Resume criteria section.
L33: 
L34: 【0†Image: Document image†cdn.images.archbee.com】
L35: 
L36: ﻿
L37: ### Add suggested criteria or previously-used criteria
L38: 
L39: Select Add from # suggestions for suggestions generated by AI based on your job posting. You can also reuse criteria from other roles you have permission to access by selecting Add previously used.
L40: 
L41: To add a suggestion, select Add in the Action column.
L42: 
L43: 【1†Image: Document image†cdn.images.archbee.com】
L44: 
L45: ﻿
L46: ### Creating effective custom criteria
L47: 
L48: Selecting Add custom instead of the suggested or previously-used options allows you to create your own criteria. You'll need to define the following:
L49: 
L50:   * Short title: The name of your criterion. This appears in job settings, the application review page, and as a filter name.
L51: 
L52:   * Prompt: The instructions used to evaluate applicants. Precise and clear prompts result in better AI performance.
L53: ### Tips on criteria effectiveness
L54: 
L55: Write your criteria as if you were instructing a junior recruiter. Ensure the prompt is phrased so that any reader would reach the same conclusion.
L56: 
L57:   * Stand-alone: Criteria should be understandable without extra context. Instead of "Can assimilate feedback," use "Effectively incorporates feedback related to personal job performance."
L58: 
L59:   * Singular: Focus on one skill per requirement. Instead of "Experience in Python and AWS," create two separate criteria for each.
L66: ## Application form criteria
L67: 
L68: You can evaluate whether a candidate answered long-form application questions in the Application Form Criteria section.
L69: 
L70: Toggle the Did the Application answer the question? option for individual questions. These are added as criteria for the review process.
L71: 
L72: This check only determines if the question was answered. Blank or unrelated answers are flagged as not meeting the criteria. This is only available for long, unformatted text fields.
L73: # Step 3: Validating and reviewing criteria
L74: 
L75: Once you have set up your criteria, it must be validated. Ashby checks your prompts on two dimensions:
L76: 
L77:   * Clarity and objectivity to ensure that the criteria is clear and objective which means it can be appropriately evaluated by the AI.
L78: 
L79:   * Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) violations: the AI also scans for implicit or explicit EEO violations and flags them.
L100: # Step 4: Saving criteria and evaluating candidates
L101: 
L102: After validation is successful, select Save and Evaluate all active candidates to begin the initial evaluation. Depending on the number of candidates, this can take a few seconds to a few minutes.
L103: 
L104: You'll see a loading screen with the total number of candidates being evaluated and a progress status bar.
L105: 
L106: 【5†Image: Document image†cdn.images.archbee.com】
L107: 
L108: ﻿
L110: # Review candidate evaluations
L111: 
L112: Ashby's AI assesses candidate resumes against each specific criterion and returns an evaluation status. The status may indicate the candidate meets, does not meet, or the AI was undecided on the criterion. Evaluation results can be seen on the candidate profile, as well as in the Application Review stage of the candidate pipeline for the role.
L113: ## Viewing results on the candidate profile
L114: 
L115: View full evaluations in the Feedback tab of a candidate profile.
L116: 
L117: 【6†Image: The Feedback tab on a candidate profile displaying the AI evaluation results summary for various resume criteria.†cdn.images.archbee.com】
L118: 
L119: ﻿
L120: 
L121: Click on any criterion to see the reasoning for a status of meets, does not meet, or undecided. Select the expand all icon to see reasoning for all criteria at once.
L122: 
L123: 【7†Image: Document image†cdn.images.archbee.com】
L124: 
L125: ﻿
L126: ## Evaluation results in Application Review
L127: 
L128: Navigate to the specific job, select the Candidate Pipeline tab on the left, and click on the Application Review stage. Here, there is a column for evaluation results that provides a summary about how the candidate scored. Hover over the results row to see more details.
L129: 
L130: 【8†Image: Document image†cdn.images.archbee.com】
L131: 
L132: ﻿
L133: You can also add an AI Job Criteria Met Percentage column to see the percentage of AI criteria each candidate met. Select Add Column on the application review page and choose AI Job Criteria Met Percentage. Sort by this column to move the best-fit candidates (highest percentage) to the top of your review queue and identify the lowest-fit candidates (lowest percentage) at a glance.
L134: ## Filtering by AI criteria
L135: 
L136: You can filter candidates by their evaluation status within your pipeline stages:
L137: 
L138:   1. Select the AI Criteria Quick Filter option.
L139: 
L140:   2. Select the criteria and statuses you want to view, such as any candidate who passed or the AI was undecided on a particular criteria.
L141: 
L142: 【9†Image: Document image†cdn.images.archbee.com】
L143: 
L144: ﻿
L145: 
L146:   3. Perform bulk actions on the filtered list as needed.
L147: 
L148: # Candidate experience & opt-out
L149: ## Automated processing legal notice
L150: 
L151: You can configure a message to display to candidates who may be impacted by automated AI review processes by following the steps below.
L152: 
L153:   1. Navigate to Admin > Data Management > Data Privacy and Compliance > Privacy & Legal to configure a legal notice for candidates.
L154: 
L155:   2. Locate the Automated Processing Legal Notice section and click on the Legal Notice for All Jobs that is displayed.
L156: 
L157:   3. Configure the settings for when this message will display:
L158:   * Is Enabled?: When off, candidates do not see the notice.
L159: 
L160:   * Rule Scope: Set criteria here when you want the message to show only based on certain criteria, such as for certain jobs only. Do not add a scope if you want it to apply to all jobs.
L161: 
L162:   * Hide Evaluations if a Candidate Hasn't Seen this Legal Notice: When enabled, AI-informed evaluations are hidden in either of these cases:
L163: 
L164:   * The candidate opts out of automated processing. In this case, the AI evaluation is skipped.
L165:   * The candidate does not submit an application directly through the Ashby-hosted application form and therefore does not see the notice displayed under the Submit Application button.
L166: 
L167: 【10†Image: Job application form showing Education History fields and a highlighted AI legal notice beneath the Submit Application button.†cdn.images.archbee.com】
L168: 
L169: ﻿
L170: 
L171: Candidates who submit an application directly through the Ashby-hosted application form are deemed to have seen the notice.
L172: If Hide Evaluations is enabled, a message will display on the candidate's evaluation results that says "The candidate has not seen the legal notice required by this job."
L173: 
L174: This can happen when a candidate is added to Ashby through a path other than the Ashby-hosted job application, such as a direct referral, a manual add, the Chrome extension, or possibly Indeed Apply.
L175: 
L176:   * Page Title: The title that candidates see at the top of the notice page.
L180: Candidates see a Learn More link under the Submit Application button. Selecting this link is optional. Candidates can use it to read the notice, opt out of automated processing, or check whether they have already opted out, but they do not need to select it for their scores to be visible. You can view what this page looks like by selecting View in the top right corner when setting up the message.
L184: ## AI opt-out filters
L185: 
L186: In your candidate pipeline, you can filter to see all candidates who have opted out of AI processing by following the below steps.
L187: 
L188:   1. Navigate to the Candidate Pipeline.

L197: # AI credits

L210: # FAQ
L211: 
L212: ### If I edit my criteria, can I re-evaluate candidates?
L213: 
L214: Yes. If you edit a prompt or change criteria, select the Save and Re-Evaluate all active Job Considerations option to refresh evaluations.
L215: 
L216: ### Can I flag AI evaluations if they are incorrect?
L217: 
L218: Yes. Select the three dots in the top-right corner of an evaluation to flag it as incorrect or misleading.
L219: ### Can I add evaluations as a column in Application Review?
L220: 
L221: Yes. Select Add Column on the job's application review page and search for the Evaluations column for a summary of how each candidate scored against your AI criteria. To see a numeric percentage of criteria met, search for AI Job Criteria Met Percentage — sort by this column to rank candidates from best fit (highest percentage) to least fit (lowest).
L222: ### What permissions are needed to edit job criteria?
L223: 
L224: You must either have Elevated Access - Admin or Elevated Access - Admin Private for the specific role, or be an Organization Admin.
L225: 
L226: ### Does the AI evaluate education and work history if there is no resume?
L227: 
L228: Yes, if the information is listed on the candidate's Ashby profile, the AI considers it.
L229: ### Will I receive a notification when a candidate opts out?
L230: 
L231: There is no proactive alert sent to customers when a candidate opts out, but you can configure alerts to be sent using Ashby's reporting capabilities and the AI Opt-Out field. See 【13†Alerts】﻿ for more information.
L232: Additionally, the opt-out status is surfaced in-product: when reviewing an application, you'll see that the job criteria evaluation was skipped, along with the reason for the skip. You can also filter to view candidates who have opted out. See AI opt-out filters above for more info.
L233: ### Does AI-Assisted Application Review affect the Average Score?
L234: No. The Average Score (also referred to as the Application Review Average Score) reflects the ratings given by human reviewers during the application review process and is calculated independently from AI criteria evaluations. If Average Score appears empty, no reviewer has manually scored that application yet. To measure AI-based candidate fit, use the AI Job Criteria Met Percentage column, which shows the proportion of AI criteria met for each candidate.

L15: AI application tools often generate email addresses to manage communication themselves. For example, instead of using the candidate’s real email address, the tool might submit an address such as: example123.nnx@emailcorper.com. T his allows the AI tool to receive and respond to messages on behalf of the candidate. This often creates multiple unique email addresses for a single candidate, each serving as a separate mailbox to handle initial communication.
L16: As a result, the same candidate may appear multiple times in your pipeline as duplicate applications. However, this can create problems during the hiring process.
L17: Common issues include:
L18: 
L19:   * Recruiter emails failing to reach the candidate.
L20: 
L21:   * Duplicate candidate profiles when the tool reapplies with a slightly different generated email.
L22: 
L23:   * Confusion or concern for hiring teams reviewing suspicious email formats.
L24: If you notice that a particular job board is generating this type of traffic, you can disable it on a per-job basis. Another effective strategy is to add auto-disqualifying questions relevant to your role, which quickly filter out low-quality or automated submissions.
L25: ## How Workable identifies AI-assisted candidates
L26: 
L27: Workable detects AI-assisted applications by analyzing application metadata and identifying patterns commonly associated with automated application tools.
L28: 
L29: Once a candidate applies to a Workable job that triggers the blacklist attributes, the following happens:
L30:   * The candidate is tagged as AI-assisted.
L31:   * If a system-generated email was used during the application, Workable will replace it with the candidate’s actual email from their resume, when available.
L32: 【6†Image】
L33: ### Filtering AI-assisted candidates
L34: 
L35: You can filter your candidate list to include or exclude AI-assisted applications. The AI-assisted filter is available in the Pipeline view and the Candidates page.
L36: 
L37: 【7†Image】
L38: ### Our bot-prevention measures
L39: 
L40: It’s important to distinguish between AI-assisted applications and bot-driven spam. To protect against bot applications, we use a multi-layered defense approach that includes:
L41: 
L42:   * Web Application Firewall (WAF)
L43: 
L44:   * IP reputation checks and browser integrity validation
L45: 
L46:   * Rate limiting, bot management, and CAPTCHA for suspicious traffic
L47: These measures help ensure that recruiters spend less time dealing with irrelevant submissions and more time focusing on real candidates.

L97:

L102:   * Add additional reasons for disqualification and choose their order in the list.
L103:   * Remove any reasons (even the default ones) you are not planning to use and don't need to be listed.

L1: # Understand Top Candidate Suggestions
L2: 
L3: The Intelligent Matching feature suggest candidates for a job requisition by matching candidates to the details of the job requisition.
L4: Candidate suggestions for a job requisition have four criteria that explain why a candidate is suggested. These four criteria, Profile, Education, Experience and Skills, provide a representation of a candidate’s job application. Hiring managers and recruiters can get a more nuanced understanding of how the candidate’s job application matches the given job. Each criteria is represented by 0-3 stars indicating the relative match, with 0 indicating no match.
L5: The artificial intelligence models use these fields from the candidate profile and the job requisition to suggest candidates for a job:
L6: Field Types  | Candidate Profile Fields  | Job Requisition Fields
L7: --- | --- | ---
L8: Title  | Concatenates all titles in the profile  | Requisition Title
L9: Experience  |
L10:   * Skill (Skill Center Section)
L11:   * Description (Skill Center Section)
L12:   * License or Certificate
L13:   * Title (Previous Employment)
L14:   * Issued By
L15:   * Degrees
L16:   * Major
L17:   * Education Level (Education)
L18:   * Job Title (Previous Employment)
L19:   * Responsibilities (Previous Employment)
L20:   * Achievements (Previous Employment)
L21:  |
L22: 
L23:   * Posting Description
L24:   * Education Level
L25:   * Job Function
L26:   * Job Family
L27:   * Qualifications
L28:   * Responsibilities
L29: This table lists the criteria against which candidates are assigned stars, along with the fields from the candidate’s profile that are used to derive the number of stars.
L30: Criteria  | Description
L31: --- | ---
L32: Profile  | Considers the title and description in the candidate’s profile.
L33: Skills  | Considers skill data from skills fields as well as keywords found through machine learning.
L34: Experience  | Considers the candidate's number of years of experience. It uses contextual words to assess the likelihood that the candidate is a manager.
L35: Education  | Considers the candidate’s most recent education.
L36: So, for example, if a candidate’s title and description have a strong match to the job requisition, the candidate is assigned 3 stars on profile. Candidate suggestions and the four criteria displayed are relative indicators that you can use to assess a candidate's application to a given job requisition. For example, if a PHD is a requirement for a job, looking at matches that have 3 stars for education can assist in the overall sourcing process.
L37: 
L38: Note:
L39: The suggested candidates and the stars don’t replace the general hiring process or the need to review a candidate in more detail. For example, you've to continue to look through the resumes of the suggested candidates before taking next steps.

L15: ## Keyword Search
L16: 
L17: When you search for candidates, you can enter a keyword in the Search field. As you enter letters in the Search field, words matching the characters you typed are displayed. The list continues to narrow as you enter more characters. You can select an item from the list and click the Search icon.
L18: 
L19: Keywords are searched in the following fields of the candidate file:
L20: 
L21:   * Candidate Number
L22: 
L23:   * Degree
L24: 
L25:   * Employer Name
L26: 
L27:   * Full Name
L28: 
L29:   * Job Title
L30: 
L31:   * Language
L32: 
L33:   * Last Name
L34: 
L35:   * License
L36:   * Major
L37: 
L38:   * Medium
L39: 
L40:   * Resume Text (resumes containing footers aren't parsed)
L41: 
L42:   * School
L43: 
L44:   * Skill
L45: 
L46:   * Source
L47: 
L48: If you search for a candidate by entering their full name in the Keyword Search field, the search results will display candidates having the same full name at the top of the results list. Candidates having the same first name or last name will be displayed after them.
L49: ## Boolean Search
L50: 
L51: A boolean search is a type of search where you can combine keywords with operators such as AND, OR, NOT, and parenthesis to produce more relevant results.
L52: 
L53: When you do a boolean search, consider the following:
L54: 
L55:   * AND, OR, NOT and parenthesis "()" are the supported boolean operators.
L56: 
L57:   * You can search in different languages but the boolean operators remain the same (AND, OR and NOT).
L58:   * Anything between the operators will be considered as a full quoted text. Example: business analyst AND "marketing manager" is the same as business analyst AND marketing manager.
L59: 
L60:   * Wild card searches "*" aren't supported.
L61: 
L62:   * Multi-level parenthesis aren't supported. Example: (manager AND (analyst OR associate)) isn't supported. But manager AND (analyst OR associate) AND (computer OR electronics) is supported.
L63: 
L64: The table provides a detailed explanation of the boolean operators and examples.
L65: Operator  | Description  | Example
L66: --- | --- | ---
L67: AND  | Use the AND operator to join keywords or different aspects of search. Use AND to find candidate profiles that include both search phrases. When you use AND in a search, it essentially narrows your results to the intersection of the two search phrases or terms. Every candidate profile result will contain both terms and typically limits your search results.  | product marketing AND manager business AND economics sales AND marketing
L71: ## Advanced Search Criteria
L72: 
L73: When you search for candidates, you can use these advanced search criteria to narrow down your search results and improve the quality of your results:
L74: 
L75:   * Candidate Details: Name, Language, Skill, Contact Info, Source, Source Medium
L76: 
L77:   * Location: Postal Code, Location
L78: 
L79:   * Education: School, Degree, Major
L80: 
L81:   * Experience: License, Job Title, Years of Experience
L82: 
L83:   * Company: Current Company, Past Company
L84: When you use an advanced search criteria, the Total Candidates number is updated. When you see a * (star) next to the Total Candidates number, it indicates that advanced search criteria were used.
L85: 
L86: Advanced search criteria are saved within the same session. If you search candidates using a criteria, go to some other screen and come back, the criteria will still be available in that session.
L87: ## LinkedIn Search
L88: You can find more candidates using LinkedIn’s search functionality, which is embedded in the Candidate Search page. L23: # Co-pilot: Candidate screening
L24: 
L25: Quickly identify strong candidates with automatic matching against your set criteria
L26: 
L27: August 27, 2026
L28: 
L29: A Company Admin user needs to activate Co-pilot in the 【5†Add-on feature center】 to get started.
L30: ​
L31: Once activated, the Candidate screening feature can be toggled on/off under Settings → Recruitment → Co-pilot → Candidate insights.
L32: 
L33: Note that the screening criteria are added using the 【6†Triggers】 feature.
L34: This feature helps streamline your recruitment process by evaluating candidates against the criteria you set. This allows you to make informed decisions faster and focus on the top applications.
L35: # Set up screening criteria
L36: 
L37: Screening criteria can be configured for any stage of your recruitment process. This allows you to screen candidates when they first apply and re-screen them later on using different criteria. For example, you can evaluate a candidate against new requirements after a conducted interview.
L38: 
L39: To add screening, open the job in question and click the three dots on the desired stage. Here, select Screen candidate under Triggers.
L40: Only user roles with editing rights to the job can set this up. Read more about the user role permissions 【7†here】.
L41: 
L42: Start by either clicking + Add criteria to create your own criteria or asking Co-pilot by choosing Suggest criteria.
L43: ## Add your own criteria
L44: 
L45: If you want to create a custom criterion, select + Add criteria.
L46: 
L47:   * Title: Choose a short, clear name that describes what the criterion is about. The title does not affect how it is evaluated.
L48: 
L49:   * Prompt: The prompt is the most important part of the criterion. It’s what Co-pilot uses to evaluate responses, so make sure it clearly describes what should be assessed.
L50: 
L51: Here are some examples of criteria:
L52: 
L53:   * Title: Computer Science education
L54: Prompt: Holds a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science.
L55: 
L56:   * Title: Based in San Francisco
L57: 
L58: Prompt: Resides in San Francisco or is willing to relocate.
L59: 
L60:   * Title: Driver's license
L61: 
L62: Prompt: Holds a valid driver's license.
L63: ## Ask Co-pilot to suggest criteria
L64: 
L65: If you select Suggest criteria, Co-pilot analyzes the job description and suggests relevant criteria for you to use or adjust.
L66: ## Verify criteria
L67: 
L68: After adding all criteria, Co-pilot will verify them before you can save the trigger. This helps ensure your prompts are set up correctly and will work as intended.
L69: 
L70: A message will appear if a prompt may be considered discriminatory or requires further clarification. For example, if a prompt simply says "Has experience," the system will make a new suggestion. Then you can choose to apply the suggestion or keep the current prompt.
L71: Once you’re finished, click Add trigger, and Co-pilot will evaluate all candidates added to the stage.
L72: # View criteria evaluations
L73: 
L74: Co-pilot evaluates the candidates against your set criteria based on the following data:
L75: 
L76:   * Resume text (supported file formats: "docx", "pptx", "pdf", "pages", "txt", "rtf")
L77: 
L78:   * Cover letter
L79: 
L80:   * Answers to the job application questions (supported question types: Range, Boolean, Choice, Text, Number, Date)
L81: 
L82:   * 【8†Comments】 connected to the job
L83: 
L84:   * 【9†Candidate address】
L85: 
L86:   * 【10†Candidate tags】
L87: 
L88:   * 【11†Candidate custom fields】 (private custom fields are excluded)
L89: When any of these data points are updated on the candidate, the screening will run again in the background.
L90: 
L91: Co-pilot only sets "✓" or "✕" when there is sufficient information to support the evaluation. When information is missing or ambiguous, a "–" icon will be displayed along with the reasoning so you can make the final assessment.
L92: ## Job process
L93: 
L94: Once the criteria have been added, the evaluation will appear on the candidate card preview in the stage. The evaluations will also be shown when enabling the Expanded view.
L95: 
L96: A quick overview of the criteria marked with "✓" or "✕" is shown here. To view the full breakdown, including any unknown criteria, open the 【12†candidate card】.
L97: ### Sort based on criteria
L98: 
L99: You can sort candidates in the stage so that those who meet the most criteria appear at the top, highlighting your top candidates.
L100: ​
L101: 
L102: To do this, click the three dots in the stage and go to Sort → Screening criteria.
L103: 
L104: Help us improve Co-pilot
L105: 
L106: Share your feedback on the help you received from Co-pilot directly in the platform. Your input will help us make your experience even better!
L107: ### Compare candidates
L108: 
L109: If you’re using the 【13†Compare candidates】 feature, the screening criteria and evaluations will be included in the data table, so you can compare candidates side by side.
L110: ​
L111: ## Candidate card
L112: 
L113: On the candidate card, you’ll find a Screening criteria section where you can view Co-pilot’s evaluation and manually override the result if needed.
L114: 
L115: Each criterion displays the evaluation status, Co-pilot’s reasoning, and a Change evaluation dropdown for any manual adjustments that may be needed. The dropdown includes the following three options:
L116: 
L117:   * Meets criteria
L118: 
L119:   * Doesn’t meet criteria
L120: 
L121:   * Unknown / Insufficient data

L123: 
L124: You can use the 【14†Smart move】 trigger to automatically move candidates to another stage based on the results of Co-pilot's evaluation of your selected screening criteria.

L24: 
L25: Identify what's missing from a candidate's application, send them a short questionnaire, and save their answers to the relevant fields in their profile
L26: 
L27: August 27, 2026
L28: 
L29: A Company Admin user needs to activate Co-pilot in the 【5†Add-on feature center】 to get started.
L30: 
L31: Note that the feature is set up using the 【6†Triggers】 feature.
L32: With the Request missing info trigger, Co-pilot identifies information missing from a candidate's profile based on the information you've selected as important for processing their job application. It then sends the candidate a questionnaire asking them to provide the missing information.
L33: ​
L34: 
L35: Once the candidate responds, their answers are automatically added to their profile. Screening criteria can then be re-evaluated, and relevant fields and personal information are updated based on the new data.
L36: # Set up a trigger
L37: 
L38: Missing information can be requested at any stage of your recruitment process. This helps ensure candidate applications are complete and ready for you and your team to review.
L39: 
L40: Open the job in question and click the three dots on the stage where you want to add the trigger. Under Triggers, select Request missing info.
L41: The Request missing info trigger is especially powerful when combined with the Smart move trigger based on 【7†screening criteria】. Together, these features can help automate your screening workflow by collecting missing information from candidates, evaluating their responses, and automatically moving them to the assigned stage based on the results.
L42: ## What to ask about
L43: 
L44: You can choose which types of information Co-pilot should look for. Missing information can be identified across the following four sections:
L45: 
L46: Application questions
L47: 
L48: Unanswered questions from the application form, either when applying or for candidates who have been sourced.
L49: 
L50: Screening criteria
L51: 【7†Screening criteria】 added to the stage that couldn't be evaluated based on the information currently available, or where additional information is needed to determine whether the candidate meets the criteria.
L52: 
L53: Custom fields
L54: 
L55: Empty 【8†candidate custom fields】 that have Automatic updates enabled.
L56: 
L57: Fields that are already covered by a question selected in another section are greyed out, so candidates aren't asked for the same information twice in one questionnaire.
L58: 
L59: Personal information
L60: Missing details from the candidate profile, including:
L61: 
L62:   * Phone number
L63: 
L64:   * Address
L65: 
L66:   * LinkedIn profile
L67: 
L68:   * Resume

L70: Co-pilot will not ask candidates for age, nationality, marital status, health information, or other information that cannot lawfully be used to support a hiring decision.
L71: ## Maximum questions
L72: 
L73: Set the maximum number of questions that can be generated in each questionnaire. This limit applies across all four sections combined.
L74: 
L75: If a resume is missing, the candidate will always be asked to upload one first. Co-pilot then works through the selected sections in the order shown above, generating questions until the maximum number is reached.
L76: ## Email
L77: 
L78: Add the email subject and message that you want to send with the questionnaire.
L79: 
L80: You can use the following placeholders:
L81: 
L82:   * `{first-name}`
L83: 
L84:   * `{last-name}`
L85: 
L86:   * `{job-title}`
L87: 
L88:   * `{company-name}`
L89: # Candidate information updates
L90: 
L91: Once the candidate submits their answers, the information is automatically added to their profile. Depending on what was requested:
L92: 
L93:   * Screening criteria are re-evaluated.
L94: 
L95:   * Custom fields are updated if empty.
L96: 
L97:   * Personal information and resume are added if missing.
L98: 
L99: This ensures the candidate's profile contains the information needed to continue the screening and recruitment process.

L23: # Co-pilot: Privacy and Security
L24: 
L25: We have summarized the frequently asked questions regarding the usage of the Teamtailor Co-pilot feature
L26: 
L27: Updated over 3 weeks ago
L28: 
L29: Co-pilot is a set of features in Teamtailor, powered by OpenAI's GPT AI models, that helps you with your daily recruiting tasks.
L114: ## Can a candidate choose whether their personal data will be used in Co-pilot?
L115: 
L116: For many of the Co-pilot features, candidate personal data is not at all processed when the feature is used - as you can see above. In the features where candidate personal data is used, the following applies:
L117: 
L118:   * Ask Co-pilot: The candidate data listed in the section above will automatically be accessed by Co-pilot for all candidates. Candidates can't opt out of this while being stored in the account.
L119:   * Candidate screening: Screening criteria can be configured for any stage of the recruitment process. When a candidate enters a stage with screening enabled, Co-pilot automatically evaluates the candidate against the configured criteria. Candidates cannot opt out of this evaluation.
L120: 
L121:   * Candidate suggestions: If you let candidates choose whether to give a “future jobs permission” or not, only candidates who have given a future jobs permission will be suggested in the feature.
L122:   * Interview kit answers: Candidates can choose not to give their consent for an interview to be recorded. When an interview is not recorded, the interview kit questions will not be completed by Co-pilot. You can delete an already generated summary.
L123: 
L124:   * Meeting insights: Candidates can choose not to give their consent for an interview to be recorded when using the Teamtailor video meeting service. When an interview is not recorded, it will not be transcribed or summarized by Co-pilot.
L125:   * Rejection email drafts: The candidate can’t choose whether to receive a drafted message by Co-pilot or not. But your users can decide whether to send a Co-pilot drafted message to particular candidates or not.
L126: 
L127:   * Resume summaries: When an application is received, the resume is automatically summarized by Co-pilot. A candidate cannot opt out of this, but you can delete an already generated summary.
L128:   * Request missing info: When a user asks Co-pilot to request missing information from a candidate, Co-pilot processes the candidate data listed in the section above to determine what information is missing and help generate the request. The feature only sends whether the candidate's phone number, address, LinkedIn profile, or resume is missing or not, and does not send the actual values. Candidates cannot opt out of this processing.

L65: ### Combine application rules using AND/OR
L66: 
L67: You can enhance the power of your application rules using AND/OR Conditions. This allows you to create rules based on multiple criteria. For example, you can create a rule based on a single answer to multiple questions or multiple answers to a single question.
L68: 
L69: Example: You can create an Auto-Advance rule that requires the candidate to have 1-2, 3-5, OR 10+ years experience AND live in a specified city.
L70: #### AND conditions
L71: 
L72: AND conditions allow you to base an application rule on the candidate's responses to multiple custom job post questions. In order to trigger the application rule, the candidate must provide one matching answer for each of the questions included in the application rule. Each application rule supports joining up to five custom questions using AND Conditions.
L73: 
L74: Note: AND conditions cannot require a candidate to select two options within the same custom job post question.
L75: For example, you include the following multi-select custom job post question: "In what programming languages are you proficient?" The candidate won't be required to select both Ruby AND Python as responses. Auto-Advance will trigger as long as the candidate selects either option for that question.
L76: 
L77: 【20†Image: Screenshot-of-add-a-rule-with-multiple-rules.png】
L78: 
L79: An AND condition can be added to a new or existing application rule.
L80: To add an AND condition when creating a new application rule, begin by following the steps to create an 【14†Auto-Tag】, 【15†Auto-Advance】, or 【16†Auto-Reject】 application rule, then continue with the steps below.
L81: 
L82: To add an AND condition to an existing application rule, navigate to the job post's Rules page using the 【9†steps outlined here】. Then, click the Edit icon inline with the Application Rule.
L83: 
L84: 【21†Image: Screenshot-of-edit-application-rule.png】
L85: From the Add a Rule dialog box, click Add another trigger.
L86: 
L87: 【22†Image: Screenshot-of-add-another-trigger-button.png】
L88: 
L89: Use the Question dropdown to select another custom question from the job post. Use the Answer dropdown to define which candidate response(s) should trigger the application rule.
L90: 
L91: 【23†Image: Screenshot-of-second-trigger-application-rule.png】
L92: Example: In the image above, candidates who respond they have 10+ years of experience and are available to work in San Francisco will be Auto-Advanced to the Preliminary Phone Screen Stage.
L93: 
L94: Candidates who respond they are available to work in San Francisco but have less than 10 years of experience will not be Auto-Advanced. These candidates will remain in the Application Review stage awaiting manual review unless Auto-Advanced or Auto-Rejected by a different Application Rule.
L95: Repeat these steps to add up to five custom questions to the application rule. When you're finished adding custom job post questions, click Save.
L96: 
L97: To remove an AND Condition from an application Rule, click the X to the right of the condition, then click Save.
L98: 
L99: 【24†Image: Screenshot-of-delete-additional-trigger-application-rule.png】
L100: Note: If an application rule uses an AND condition to include two custom job post questions and one of the questions is deleted from the job post, the application rule will be based on the remaining job post question only. If an application rule is based on a single custom job post question and that question is deleted from the job post, the application rule will also be removed.
L101: #### OR conditions
L102: 
L103: OR conditions allow you to base an application rule on multiple possible responses to a single custom job post question. The candidate only needs to select one of the possible responses to trigger the application rule.
L104: 
L105: Example: You can create an Auto-Advance rule for the multi-select custom job post question In which programming languages are you proficient? that advances candidates who select Ruby OR Python.
L106: To configure an OR condition, begin by following the steps to create an 【14†Auto-Tag】, 【15†Auto-Advance】, or 【16†Auto-Reject】 application rule, then continue with the steps below.
L107: 
L108: To add an OR condition to an existing application rule, navigate to the job post's Rules page using the 【9†steps outlined here】 and click the Edit icon inline with the application rule.
L109: In the Answer dropdown for an existing or additional custom job post question, enter each candidate response that should trigger the Application Rule. When you're finished adding options, click Save.
L110: 
L111: 【25†Image: Screenshot-of-OR-rule-creation.png】
L112: Note: If an OR condition rule is based on either of two custom job post question responses and one of the responses is deleted from the custom job post question, the rule will be based on only the remaining custom job post question response. If an OR condition rule is based on a single custom job post question response and that response is deleted from the custom job post question, the question will be removed from the application rule.
L113: ### Application rules expected behavior
L114: 
L115: In this section, we will discuss expected behaviors when using application rules, as well as review scenarios where application rules overlap with one another.
L116: #### Auto-advance behaviors
L117: 
L118:   * If an Auto-Advance rule moves a candidate to a given stage and that stage later is removed from the job's Interview Plan, the Auto-Advance rule will update to instead advance the candidate to the stage preceding the now-deleted stage. A user can edit the Auto-Advance rule to advance the candidate to an alternative stage if preferred.
L119: Example: If an Auto-Advance rule advances candidates to the Face to Face stage in the following Interview Plan, and that stage is deleted, the Auto-Advance rule will advance candidates to the Take Home Test stage instead:
L120: Application Review > Phone Screen > Take Home Test > Face to Face > Offer
L121:   * If an Auto-Advance rule is configured for a job post and the job post is sent to a candidate as a 【26†job post request email】, the candidate will not be Auto-Advanced based on their responses. Auto-Reject rules associated with the job post will not be applied to the candidate's responses either. However, Auto-Tags associated with the job post will be applied.
L125:   * Auto-Tag rules always will be applied, regardless of any other Application Rules that might be triggered.
L126:   * Only one Auto-Advance or Auto-Reject rule will ever be applied to a single candidate. If both an Auto-Advance and an Auto-Reject rule are triggered, the Auto-Reject rule will be applied.

L61: #### When does fraud detection run in the application flow?
L62: 
L63: Spam and IP blocklists (org-level) run before fraud checks. If an application is rejected as spam, a fraud report is not run. Fraud detection runs after other application hygiene steps (e.g., auto-reject rules, automerge, application limits)
L111: #### Who can access the Fraud Detection signals in the Greenhouse application?
L112: 
L113: Access is controlled via dedicated permission stripes for Job Admins for both read access and running a fraud report.
L114: #### How do Greenhouse and IPQS protect Fraud signal data?
L115: 
L116: Data is protected in transit using TLS 1.2+ and is protected at rest by both Greenhouse and IPQS. Greenhouse adheres to a strict data minimization policy and IPQS is configured for zero day data retention to only process but not store customer data.
L117: Access to Greenhouse data is protected by safeguards such as multi-factor access controls that include device trust. Access to the console is very limited, requiring two levels of approval and quarterly access reviews. Staff members with access to this data must successfully complete a background check before being granted access to any customer data.
L118: Additionally, all staff members with customer data access must agree to our written zero-tolerance policy, which defines their responsibilities and the consequences (including, but not limited to, termination of employment) of abusing their access. Both Greenhouse and IPQS undergo annual SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 audits to validate that our organizational security controls are operating as expected.

L54: ## A new way of working
L55: 
L56: So how did I accurately and confidently review 1,500 resumes in 6 hours? By changing the mental model and approach with the help of our new feature.
L57: 
L58: Everything leading up stays the same — I learn the job description inside and out and qualify the role. But now, using Ashby's AI-Assisted Application Review feature, I document a series of specific criteria that applicants should meet.
L59: 
L60: 【7†Image: defining criteria】
L87: This naturally creates a feedback loop with the quality of the job description. If unsuitable talent is coming through, it signals the need to refine the criteria and improve the job description to reflect that.
L88: Understandably, adopting this technology into your process comes with a healthy dose of “What about...?” Whether it's regulation, introducing biases, or in-product controls, there’s a lot to consider. To help talent teams embrace this kind of advanced technology, we’ve given as much thought to addressing these concerns as we have to the functionality of the feature.
L89: To see the full picture of everything we’re doing to prevent bias, comply with regulations, and provide peace of mind for your team when using this feature, head over to 【12†the product blog post】.
L90: ## What does this mean for candidates?
L91: 
L92: The job of the candidate remains the same as it has always been in the application process: clearly communicate, through your resume and application, how you meet the minimum requirements in the job description.
L93: The same reviewer actions—advancing or rejecting—are being taken. The AI assistance serves as an input to the decision-making process, not a replacement. Ultimately, talent acquisition teams are responsible for finding the best talent, and any shortcuts or blind advancing/rejecting run directly counter to that mission.
L94: When used in the way we built this feature, AI assistance reduces biases by focusing on objective, specific, and consistent criteria. It also levels the playing field for job seekers who may not have a referral or direct connection to the company they aspire to work for.
L98:   * The time saved during application reviews allows you to refocus and reallocate efforts to higher-touch activities in your recruiting process.
L99:   * AI assistance depends on reviewer decision-making. No action is taken for you, and it remains the reviewer’s responsibility to approve or reject.
L100:   * Specific, objective criteria reduce bias. Reviewers across large teams work from the same criteria analysis, eliminating the need for implicit shortcuts to handle high volumes.
L107: Properly defining criteria and processing applications introduces greater objectivity into the screening process. This creates a significant opportunity to monitor and improve your 【13†Quality of Hire】. Drawing a direct line between criteria setting and Quality of Hire is something I’m particularly excited about, and it's made possible entirely through Ashby reporting.

L0: # Auto-Reject Applications
L1: 
L2: 14 min
L3: 
L4: This guide covers how to streamline your application review process by using the auto-reject feature.
L5: # Auto-Reject overview
L6: 
L7: Auto-Reject allows you to reject candidates whose application submissions match certain conditions automatically. Rejection conditions apply to the selected application form for a given job. For example, if you have a location-based application question, you can configure a rule within the job posting to automatically reject candidates located outside of the targeted area.
L8: Auto-reject rules can only be configured to run at the point of the candidate's application submission and cannot run at other stages in the interview process.
L9: 
L10: Watch the following optional video for an overview of Auto-Reject, or follow the steps below.
L11: 
L12: ﻿
L13: # How to set up an auto-reject configuration
L14: 
L15: To set up an Auto-Reject condition:
L16: 
L17:   1. Navigate to Jobs > Jobs and select a job.
L18: 
L19:   2. Navigate to Job Postings, then click on a listing to access the posting tabs.
L20: 
L21:   3. Select the Automation tab. The tab contains job-specific automation options including automatic application confirmation emails and auto-reject.
L22: 
L23:   4. Click Create a Configuration, then configure the fields below.
L24: 【0†Image: The screenshow shows the Draft Auto-Reject Configuration page.†cdn.zappy.app】
L25: 
L26: ﻿
L27: 
L28: This screenshot highlights 6 key areas of auto-reject configuration setup:
L29: 
L30:   1. Conditions run in order. If a candidate is rejected by one condition, future conditions are skipped. If a rejection condition is empty, it is skipped.
L31:   2. The Rejection Condition is based on application questions. Select a question and configure the conditional behavior. For example, if the rejection condition is 'Application Form's Name contains A', 'Aaron' would be rejected and 'Bob' would not be.
L32: 
L33:   3. The Archive Reason is added to the candidate profile when an application is auto-rejected using the rejection condition.
L34: 
L35:   4. Configure the number of business days to delay the rejection email to candidates.
L36:   5. Select the rejection email template to send to the candidate. These must be preconfigured in Email Templates.
L37: 
L38:   6. Select the from address the rejection email is sent from.
L39: 
L40: You can click + Create New Auto-Reject Rule to create additional auto-reject rules. Ashby applies auto-reject rules to applications in the order they are listed.
L41: 
L42: 【1†Image: The screenshot shows the rejection configuration section with the Create New Auto-Reject Rule option highlighted.†cdn.zappy.app】
L43: 
L44: ﻿
L45: Once configured and activated, Auto-Reject evaluates all new applications. Auto-reject does not currently support applying the rule to historical applications.
L46: ## Setting up a Rejection Condition
L47: 
L48: When setting up your auto-reject conditions, first click Add Field to Match. You can select a question on your application form and determine the answers that trigger the auto-reject tool.
L49: 
L50: Once you've selected your question, you see the following options for determining an answer that leads to automatic rejection. This example is for a question with a multiple-choice answer field.
L51: 【2†Image: The screenshot shows a condition being configured using the equals options on an application form field. †cdn.zappy.app】
L52: 
L53: ﻿
L54: 
L55: Is empty/unassigned: No answer has been added or selected. Select this if you want to automatically reject a candidate if they have not answered the question.
L56: 
L57: Is not empty/unassigned: Any answer has been added in response to the application form. Selecting this automatically rejects any candidate who has answered the question.
L58: Equals: Select or add a value here. If the candidate has responded with the exact same answer, they are rejected automatically.
L59: 
L60: Depending on the field type, you may see additional options. Here is another example where the field type is one that can be typed into directly, rather than selecting a specific answer, as above.
L61: 
L62: 【3†Image: The screenshot shows a rejection configuration being set up using the contains option.†cdn.zappy.app】
L63: 
L64: ﻿
L65: Contains: The answer contains the text you add to the Add text to match field beside the drop-down menu. If the applicant's answer contains this text, they are rejected automatically.
L66: 
L67: Starts with: Ashby rejects the application if the answer starts with the text specified in the Add text to match field.
L68: 
L69: Ends with: Ashby rejects the application if the answer ends with the text specified in the Add text to match field.
L70: Similar to: Ashby rejects the application if the answer is similar to the text in the Add text to fuzzy match field. For example, if localization is added to the Add text to fuzzy match field and the applicant includes the word local in their application, this constitutes a fuzzy match.
L71: ## Auto-Reject operators
L72: 
L73: While configuring your auto-reject rules, you see the operators And, Or, and Not.
L74: 
L75: 【4†Image: The screenshot shows rejection conditions being configured with the auto-reject operators highlighted.†cdn.zappy.app】
L76: 
L77: ﻿
L78: And: This option adds an All are True condition to the rule, so you can set multiple conditions and, as long as all conditions are met, the candidate is rejected. In this example, the candidate is rejected if they select No for both of the specified questions. If they select Yes for one of the two, they are not rejected automatically.
L79: 
L80: 【5†Image: The screenshot shows rejection conditions with the All are true operator.†cdn.zappy.app】
L81: 
L82: ﻿
L83: Or: This option adds an Any can be True condition to the rule. If any of the conditions listed are met, the candidate's application is rejected automatically. In this example, if the candidate selects No for either question, their application is rejected automatically.
L84: 
L85: 【6†Image: The screenshot shows rejection conditions with the Any can be true operator.†cdn.zappy.app】
L86: 
L87: ﻿
L88: Not: This option adds a The following is not true condition to the form. Candidates who do not meet the criteria specified in the rules are rejected automatically. In this example, if the candidate does not select Yes as their answer to the question, they are automatically rejected.
L89: 
L90: 【7†Image: The screenshot shows rejection conditions with the The following is not true operator.†cdn.zappy.app】
L91: 
L92: ﻿
L93: You can also add these operators within one another! If you are using the Not operator and want to add multiple conditions the candidate needs to meet, select the And operator once you've set up your first condition to add another. In this example, both questions need to be answered Yes for the candidate to pass through to the Application Review stage. If a candidate answers Yes to one question and No to the other, they are rejected automatically.
L94: 【8†Image: The screenshot shows rejection conditions with the The following is not true and All are true operators.†cdn.zappy.app】
L95: 
L96: ﻿
L97: # How to edit an auto-reject configuration
L98: 
L99: When there is an active configuration and Auto-Reject is enabled, you need to create a new draft condition to make edits. The active condition continues to run until the draft condition is activated.
L100: 
L101:   1. Click View Current Configuration.
L102: 
L103:   2. Click Create a New Draft... and configure the draft condition.
L104: 
L105:   3. Click Activate.
L106: 
L107: 【9†Image: The screenshot shows an auto-reject configuration with the Create a New Draft option highlighted.†cdn.zappy.app】
L108: 
L109: ﻿
L110: # Turning off auto-reject on a job posting
L111: 
L112: To deactivate an active configuration, switch off the Auto-Reject Enabled toggle in the Automation tab of the selected job posting.
L113: 
L114: 【10†Image: The screenshot shows Auto-Reject Applications with Auto-Reject Enabled on.†cdn.zappy.app】
L115: 
L116: ﻿
L117: 
L118: Once disabled, the tag beside the Auto-Reject Application heading turns red and displays Disabled.
L119: 
L120: 【11†Image: The screenshot shows Auto-Reject Applications with Auto-Reject Enabled off.†cdn.zappy.app】
L121: 
L122: ﻿
L123: # Search for candidates that have been auto-rejected
L124: 
L125: If you'd like to review rejected candidates, you can find all archived candidates within the candidate pipeline of your job in the Archived view. You can then add an advanced filter to display only auto-rejected candidates.
L126: 
L127: 【12†Image: The screenshot shows a job with the Archived section of the timeline open.†cdn.zappy.app】
L128: 
L129: ﻿
L130: 
L131: To search for those candidates:
L132: 
L133:   1. Navigate to the Archived candidates view in the candidate pipeline.
L134:   2. Select the Advanced filter option.
L135: 
L136:   3. Search for the Auto-Rejected filter and set it to equal Yes.
L137: ## Auto-reject information on candidate profiles
L138: 
L139: 【13†Image: The screenshot shows the candidate's profile with the feed showing that the candidate was rejected by Ashby Bot.†cdn.zappy.app】
L140: 
L141: ﻿
L142: 
L143: This screenshot highlights two key auto-reject activities on the candidate profile:
L144: 
L145:   1. For delayed emails, you find a Scheduled Email activity under Current Activities. You have the option to view the scheduled email, modify it, or delete it.
L146:   2. In the feed, you find a notification that the candidate was moved to the Archived stage by Ashby Bot.
L147: # FAQ
L148: 
L149: ### How do auto-reject rules interact with application requests?
L150: 
L151: If an application is submitted through an application request link, Ashby does not check those applications against auto-reject or application limit rules.
L152: 
L153: ### Can I reject candidates who have applied multiple times?
L154: 
L155: You can set up application limits if you are seeing candidates apply multiple times for the same role or department. More on configuring these at 【14†Application Limits】Application Limits.
L156: ### Can I configure auto-reject rules for interview stages?
L157: 
L158: No, auto-reject rules can only be configured on the job posting and so will only be applied to applications at the point of submission via your job board.
L159: ### I'm unable to select an archive reason when configuring auto-reject. Why?
L160: 
L161: Organization Admins have access to Archive Reasons by default. Users with Elevated Access roles do not automatically inherit this permission, so it needs to be granted separately under their Additional User Permissions. More on this at 【15†Additional User Permissions】﻿.

L23: # Co-pilot: Resume summaries

L26: 
L27: August 27, 2026
L28: 
L29: A Company Admin user needs to activate Co-pilot in the 【5†Add-on feature center】 to get started.
L30: ​
L31: Once activated, the Resume summaries feature can be toggled on/off under Settings → Recruitment → Co-pilot → Candidate insights.
L32: With this feature, Co-pilot automatically summarizes the candidate’s resume into a five-point bullet list displayed in the Resume section, helping you focus on the most important information when screening candidates.
L33: # Resume summary
L34: 
L35: The resume summary will exclude any identifying details about the candidate, such as their name, email address, gender, or other personal information. Co-pilot will summarize the most recently uploaded resume on their candidate profile.
